mainTopic: The seventy years of exile and כורש's role, followed by a phrase-by-phrase reading of אחשורוש's feast in the first chapter of the מגילה.
overview: This עמוד starts by finishing the count of the seventy years of exile. A ברייתא shows that one year was still missing after בלשאצר, and רבא shows that even דניאל miscalculated. Two פסוקים seem to count the seventy years from different starting points. רבא explains that the count 'for בבל' ended only with פקידה, כורש's permission to return. A side teaching explains that God complained to משיח that כורש only let the Jews go up and did not rebuild. The גמרא then goes back to the opening פסוקים of the מגילה. It explains why פרס and מדי switch order, says that אחשורוש wore the בגדי כהונה, and records whether he was clever or foolish to feast the faraway guests first. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי explains that the Jews deserved destruction for bowing to the idol, but only for show, so ה׳ only threatened them. The גמרא then explains the feast's seating, fabrics, couches, floor stones, cups and wine, and the roles of מרדכי and המן. It ends with ושתי's feast in the royal house, and רבא's folk saying about it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports that one year was still missing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one more year of בבל's seventy was left after בלשאצר, and דריוש completed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: There was still one more year left for בבל, and דריוש arose and completed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up what it was just saying: the seventy years were not truly finished when בלשאצר thought they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion explained that בלשאצר's count was off, because the years he counted were not all full years. The ברייתא confirms this: even after בלשאצר, one more year of בבל's seventy still had to pass. That year was finished only under דריוש.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא). This brings support from an outside teaching.
דריוש, the king who ruled after בלשאצר
And he completed it, meaning he finished the last missing year

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
and there was still another year for Babylonia
phrases.notes: Even after בלשאצר was killed, one year of בבל's seventy was still left.

phrases.english: and Darius arose and completed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the argument earlier that the seventy-year count was not complete in בלשאצר's time.
steps.raayaObject: That the seventy years for בבל were not finished at בלשאצר's death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that one more year remained, and דריוש completed it.

steps.title: Even דניאל miscalculated the seventy years
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves from the word 'בינותי' that דניאל, too, had once made a mistake in this count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even דניאל made a mistake in this calculation. It says, 'In the first year of his reign, I, דניאל, meditated in the books.' Since he says 'I meditated', we can learn that he had made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds that בלשאצר was not the only one confused by this count. Even דניאל got it wrong at first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בינותי' means 'I thought it over carefully' or 'I worked it out again'. You only need to recalculate if your first calculation was off. So רבא reads the word as a sign that דניאל had made a mistake earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: I considered carefully, I worked it out again
From this we can learn that... It introduces an inference.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how difficult the seventy-year calculation was. Even a נביא like דניאל had to recalculate it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even Daniel erred in this calculation,
as it is written: "In the first year of his reign
phrases.notes: This is from דניאל chapter 9. The פסוק goes on to talk about the seventy years for the ruins of ירושלים.

phrases.english: I, Daniel, meditated in the books."
From the fact that he said "I meditated,"
it can be inferred that he had erred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף דָּנִיאֵל טְעָה בְּהַאי חוּשְׁבָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that this counting mistake also happened to דניאל, not only to בלשאצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דניאל also erred in calculating the seventy years. This is learned from his word 'בינותי'.

steps.title: Two פסוקים seem to count the seventy years differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק counts seventy years 'for בבל' and another counts seventy years 'for the ruins of ירושלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the פסוקים contradict each other. One says 'seventy years are completed for בבל', and another says 'for the ruins of ירושלים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem: two פסוקים seem to give two different starting points for the seventy years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיה counts the seventy years from בבל's rule, which began before the destruction. The פסוק in דניאל counts them from the destruction of ירושלים. These two starting points are years apart, so it seems the two counts cannot end at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, regardless of what was just said

phrases.english: In any case, the verses contradict each other,
it is written: "are accomplished for Babylonia,"
phrases.notes: This is ירמיה 29:10: 'when seventy years are completed for בבל, I will remember you.'

phrases.english: and it is written: "for the desolations of Jerusalem"!
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק in דניאל quoted a moment ago. It counts from the destruction of ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק in דניאל just quoted and sets it against the פסוק in ירמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the פסוקים in ירמיה and דניאל about the seventy years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק counts seventy years from בבל's rule and the other from ירושלים's destruction. These are different starting points, so the counts seem to clash.

steps.title: The seventy years for בבל only end with being 'remembered'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the seventy years for בבל end only with פקידה, the first step of permission to return.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The seventy years for בבל were just for being 'remembered'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the contradiction. The two counts lead to two different events, so they do not need to end at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיה says that after seventy years for בבל 'I will remember (אפקוד) you'. רבא says this count only leads to that first step of being remembered, meaning permission to go back. The count for the ruins of ירושלים is a separate count that leads to the actual rebuilding.

keyTerms.meaning: Being remembered, attended to. Here it means the first step of redemption, permission to return.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying one of the פסוקים is wrong. Both counts are correct. They simply mark the end of two different stages.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It was only for being remembered.
phrases.notes: He is playing off the word in ירמיה's פסוק, 'I will remember you'. The בבל count only brings that first step, not the full rebuilding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two פסוקים: each refers to a different endpoint.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe the same seventy years ending at the same event.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventy years for בבל end with פקידה (permission to return). The seventy years for ירושלים's ruins are a separate count that leads to the actual rebuilding.

steps.title: כורש's announcement proves the meaning of פקידה
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his answer with כורש's words, 'He has charged (פקד) me to build Him a house in ירושלים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it says: 'Thus says כורש, king of פרס‎: ה׳, God of heaven, gave me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build Him a house in ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a פסוק from עזרא to show that the 'remembering' happened when כורש gave permission to return and begin building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כורש's announcement uses the same root word, פקד, as ירמיה's 'I will remember you'. This shows that the end of בבל's seventy years matches כורש's permission, the first stage. It was not yet the finished בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written. It brings a פסוק that fits the point just made.
כורש, king of פרס, who allowed the Jews to return
He charged me, appointed me (the same root as פקידה)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two different seventy-year counts. The count from בבל's rule ended with כורש's permission to return, called 'פקידה'. The count from the destruction of ירושלים is a separate count, leading to the actual rebuilding.

phrases.english: And this is as it is written:
"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia:
phrases.notes: This is the opening of ספר עזרא, where כורש lets the Jews go back.

phrases.english: All the kingdoms of the earth has given me
the Lord, God of heaven,
and He has charged me
phrases.notes: This is the key word: פקד, the same root as 'I will remember you' in ירמיה.

phrases.english: to build Him a house in Jerusalem."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support רבא's answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the end of the seventy years for בבל meant פקידה, permission to return.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 1:2, where כורש says 'פקד עלי לבנות לו בית בירושלים'.

steps.title: Was כורש really called God's anointed one?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא quotes a פסוק that seems to call כורש God's משיח and asks how that can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'So says ה׳ to His anointed one, to כורש, whose right hand I held'? Was כורש really the משיח?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last step mentioned כורש, the גמרא brings a teaching about him. It starts with a puzzle: a פסוק seems to call כורש 'God's anointed one'. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'לִמְשִׁיחוֹ לְכוֹרֶשׁ' sounds like כורש himself is the משיח. A non-Jewish king who did not even finish building the בית המקדש cannot be the משיח. So the plain reading has to be wrong, and a new reading is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught a lesson drawn from a פסוק
'Is it really so that...?', a question showing something can't be right

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught from a verse:
What is the meaning of what is written:
phrases.notes: The פסוק comes from ישעיהו 45:1.

phrases.english: "So says ה׳ to His anointed one, to Cyrus,
whose right hand I have held"?
Now, was Cyrus the Messiah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up on the mention of כורש in Step 5 and brings another teaching about him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of ישעיהו 45:1, which seems to call כורש 'His anointed one'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כורש cannot be the משיח, so the פסוק cannot mean that God is speaking to כורש as His anointed one.

steps.title: God complains to משיח about כורש
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is read as הקב״ה speaking to משיח about כורש: כורש was supposed to build the בית המקדש and gather the exiles, but he only gave permission to go up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, הקב״ה said to משיח: 'I am complaining to you about כורש. I said he would build My House and gather My exiles, and all he said was: Whoever among you is from His people, let him go up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the puzzle by reading the פסוק differently. God is speaking to משיח, and the topic is כורש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'לִמְשִׁיחוֹ' means 'to the משיח', and 'לְכוֹרֶשׁ' means 'about כורש'. The complaint is that God planned for כורש to rebuild the בית המקדש and bring everyone home. כורש only gave permission to anyone who wanted to go back (עזרא 1:3). This fits Step 5, where כורש's role was only the first step, the פקידה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will gather My exiles

steps.whatToRemember: כורש opened the door for the return, but he did not finish the job God intended for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמָשִׁיחַ:
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Messiah:
I am complaining to you about Cyrus.
I said: He will build My House
phrases.notes: This is drawn from ישעיהו 45:13, where God says כורש will build His city.

phrases.english: and gather My exiles,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא אָמַר: ״מִי בָכֶם מִכׇּל עַמּוֹ וְיַעַל״.
phrases.english: but he said: "Whoever is among you of all His people, let him go up."
phrases.notes: These are כורש's own words in עזרא 1:3. He only allowed people to go, nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמָשִׁיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 by giving a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק: 'to His anointed one' means to משיח, and 'to כורש' means about כורש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק calls כורש God's משיח.
steps.terutzMaskana: God is speaking to משיח and complaining that כורש did only part of what he was meant to do.

steps.title: Why does the order of פרס and מדי switch?
steps.stepSummary: Back in the מגילה, one פסוק says 'פרס and מדי' and another says 'מדי and פרס'.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says 'the army of פרס and מדי, the nobles', and another says 'the kings of מדי and פרס'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to explaining פסוקים of the מגילה. It points out that the order of the two nations flips between two פסוקים, and the next step explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אסתר 1:3, about the nobles and officers, פרס comes first. In אסתר 10:2, about the kings, מדי comes first. The גמרא wants to know why the order changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Persia and Media, the two nations in אחשורוש's empire

phrases.english: "The army of Persia and Media, the nobles,"
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 1:3, the guest list for אחשורוש's first feast. פרס comes first.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Of the kings of Media and Persia."
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 10:2, near the end of the מגילה. Here מדי comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of כורש and returns to explaining the פסוקים of the מגילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The changing order of פרס and מדי in אסתר 1:3 and 10:2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two nations are always listed together, why does the order flip?

steps.title: רבא: the kings and ministers take turns
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that פרס and מדי made a deal: whichever nation supplies the king, the other supplies the ministers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They made a deal with each other. If the kings come from us, the ministers come from you, and if the kings come from you, the ministers come from us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question about the switching order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two nations shared power: when one nation supplied the king, the other supplied the ministers. So when the פסוק talks about kings, מדי comes first, and when it talks about nobles and officers, פרס comes first. Each nation comes first in the area where it held power.

phrases.english: Rava said: They made a firm agreement with each other:
If the kings come from us, the ministers come from you;
and if the kings come from you, the ministers come from us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical explanation: power was split between the two nations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The changing order looks random or unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each nation is listed first where it held power: מדי for kings, פרס for nobles.

steps.title: אחשורוש wore the בגדי כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא teaches that when אחשורוש showed off his wealth, he was wearing the בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom': רבי יוסי בר חנינא said this teaches that he wore the בגדי כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next פסוק in the מגילה, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא gives a surprising teaching about it. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes אחשורוש showing off his 'כבוד' and 'תפארת'. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says this hints that he dressed in the כהן גדול's clothes, which had been taken from the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: "When he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom":
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 1:4.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
This teaches that he wore the priestly garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלָּבַשׁ בִּגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק of the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחשורוש wore the בגדי כהונה at his feast.

steps.title: Proof from matching words: כבוד and תפארת
steps.stepSummary: The same words, כבוד and תפארת, appear both in the מגילה and in the תורה's description of the בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'the honor of his majestic greatness', and there, about the בגדי כהונה, it says 'for glory and for majesty'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching from Step 10 by showing that the same words are used in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה uses 'כבוד' and 'תפארת' for what אחשורוש showed off. The תורה (שמות 28:2) uses exactly 'לכבוד ולתפארת' for the בגדי כהונה. The matching words connect the two, so what אחשורוש showed off was the בגדי כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here... and it says there (matching words in two places)

phrases.english: It is written here: "The honor of his majestic greatness,"
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, אסתר 1:4. The first half had the word 'כבוד'.

phrases.english: and it is written there: "For glory and for majesty."
phrases.notes: This is שמות 28:2, describing the clothes of the כהן גדול.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״יְקָר תִּפְאֶרֶת גְּדוּלָּתוֹ״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״לְכָבוֹד וּלְתִפְאֶרֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the teaching of Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That אחשורוש wore the בגדי כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared words כבוד and תפארת in אסתר 1:4 and שמות 28:2

steps.title: רב and שמואל: was אחשורוש smart or foolish?
steps.stepSummary: About the second feast, held for the people of שושן, רב and שמואל disagree whether אחשורוש was a clever king or a foolish one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And when these days were over...': רב and שמואל disagree. One says he was a clever king, and one says he was a foolish king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next פסוק and states a disagreement between רב and שמואל. The reasons for each side come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחשורוש first made a long feast for the officials of the provinces. Only afterward did he make one for the people of his own city, שושן. The argument is whether this order was wise.

keyTerms.meaning: And when the days were completed
One said... and the other said

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which one, רב or שמואל, holds which opinion. It only says 'one said... and one said'.

phrases.english: "And when these days were completed, etc."
phrases.notes: This is אסתר 1:5. After the long feast, the king made a feast for everyone in שושן.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One said: He was a clever king,
and one said: He was a foolish king.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר: מֶלֶךְ פִּיקֵּחַ הָיָה, וְחַד אָמַר: מֶלֶךְ טִיפֵּשׁ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק of the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement about whether making the feast for the faraway guests first was clever or foolish.

steps.title: Why it was clever to invite the faraway people first
steps.stepSummary: The 'clever' view: it was smart to win over the faraway subjects first, since the king can please his own townspeople whenever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he was clever holds that he did well to bring the faraway people close first, because he could win over the people of his own city any time he wanted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the side that called אחשורוש clever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The faraway officials are hard to reach and easy to lose, so they need attention first. The people of שושן live right next to the king, so he can always make them happy later.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of his own city
To win over, to make peace with

phrases.english: The one who says he was a clever king holds:
he acted well in bringing close the distant ones first,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְנֵי מָאתֵיהּ כׇּל אֵימַת דְּבָעֵי מְפַיֵּיס לְהוּ.
phrases.english: since the people of his own city he can win over whenever he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion stated in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Invite the hard-to-reach people first, because the close ones are always available.

steps.title: Why it was foolish to invite the faraway people first
steps.stepSummary: The 'foolish' view: he should have won over his own townspeople first, so they would stand by him if the faraway subjects rebelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he was foolish holds that he should have brought his own townspeople close first, so that if the others rebelled against him, these would stand with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the side that called אחשורוש foolish, which ends the disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This side thinks about safety rather than reach. The people around the king are his protection. If they are loyal and the provinces rebel, the people nearby will defend him.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on what אחשורוש did. They argue only about whether it was wise: reach the far ones first (clever), or secure the near ones first (foolish).

phrases.english: And the one who says he was foolish holds:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְקָרוֹבֵי בְּנֵי מָאתֵיהּ בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: he should have brought close the people of his city first,
so that if those had rebelled against him,
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the faraway officials from the provinces.

phrases.english: these would have stood with him.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the people of שושן, who live right near the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion of Step 12, in contrast to Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Secure the loyalty of the people nearby first, so they will defend the king if the provinces rebel.

steps.title: The students ask why that generation deserved destruction
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי ask why the Jews of the פורים generation deserved כליה, and he tells them to suggest an answer first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי asked him: Why did the Jews of that generation deserve to be wiped out? He said to them: You say first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new conversation. The students ask their teacher why the Jews in the time of the מגילה deserved the terrible decree of destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the decree was a punishment for some sin, and they want to know which sin. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי turns the question back to them, a teaching method that sets up the back-and-forth that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'the enemies of Israel', a polite way of saying the Jews themselves when speaking of something bad

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of Israel' here does NOT mean the non-Jews. It is a polite way of talking about the Jews themselves, so as not to say something bad about them directly.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: The students of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai asked him:
For what reason were they deserving

phrases.aramaic: שׂוֹנְאֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר כְּלָיָה?
phrases.english: the 'enemies of Israel' in that generation, of destruction?
phrases.notes: 'Enemies of Israel' is a gentle way of saying the Jews themselves, so as not to say outright that the Jews deserved death.

phrases.english: He said to them: You say (the answer).

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the feasts in steps 10-14, though it is connected through the theme of אחשורוש's feast.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sin made the Jews of that generation deserve destruction?

steps.title: The students suggest: because they ate at the wicked king's feast
steps.stepSummary: The students answer that the Jews deserved destruction because they enjoyed אחשורוש's feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Because they enjoyed the feast of that wicked man.
steps.whatsHappening: The students give their answer. The sin was taking part in אחשורוש's party.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This links the decree to the feast described at the start of the מגילה. Joining a non-Jewish king's feast, with its forbidden food, was seen as a serious sin.

phrases.english: They said to him: Because they enjoyed
the feast of that wicked man.
phrases.notes: 'That wicked man' is אחשורוש, whose feast we have been learning about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ מִסְּעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They deserved destruction because they enjoyed אחשורוש's feast.

steps.title: The feast answer doesn't fit, because the decree was against everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי rejects the students' answer. Only the Jews of שושן were at the feast, but the decree was against Jews everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the Jews in שושן should be killed, but the Jews in the rest of the world should not be killed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי pushes back on the students' answer and shows why it can't be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment has to match the sin. The feast was only in שושן, yet המן's decree covered Jews in every country. So eating at the feast can't explain why all of them deserved destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: the capital city where the feast took place

phrases.english: If so, those in שושן should be killed,
but those in the rest of the whole world should not be killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the feast as the reason for the decree against the whole nation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sin was limited to שושן, but the decree reached Jews everywhere, so the punishment doesn't match the sin.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's answer: because they bowed to the idol
steps.stepSummary: The students ask their teacher for his answer, and he says it was because they bowed to the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You tell us! He said to them: Because they bowed down to the idol.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the teacher gives his own answer. The sin was bowing to an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sin fits the scope of the decree. Bowing to the idol (the statue of נבוכדנצר) was done by people everywhere, not only in שושן, so it can explain a decree against the whole Jewish people.

phrases.english: They said to him: You say!
He said to them: Because they bowed down to the idol.
phrases.notes: This is the statue of נבוכדנצר from ספר דניאל. Everyone bowed to it except חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the question in step 15 after the first answer was rejected in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They deserved destruction because they bowed to the idol.

steps.title: Then why were they saved? Is ה׳ playing favorites?
steps.stepSummary: The students challenge him. If they really worshipped an idol, why did ה׳ save them? Is that favoritism?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is there favoritism in this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The students raise a challenge against their teacher's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Jews committed real idol worship, they should have been punished. Being saved by a miracle would look like ה׳ showing unfair favor to them.

keyTerms.meaning: is it really so that...? (a challenging question)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וְכִי מַשּׂוֹא פָּנִים יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר?
phrases.english: They said to him: Is there favoritism in this matter?
phrases.notes: They mean: if they truly deserved death for idol worship, why were they saved in the end?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's claim that they deserved destruction for bowing to the idol.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real idol worship deserves real punishment. Saving them would be unfair favoritism, which ה׳ does not show.

steps.title: It was only for show on both sides
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers that they bowed only for show, so ה׳ only made a show of punishing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They only did it for show, so ה׳ also only acted toward them for show.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי answers the challenge. Their sin was not real, so ה׳'s punishment was not real either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They bowed outwardly out of fear of the king, but did not truly believe in the idol. So ה׳ matched them measure for measure. He issued a frightening decree but did not carry it out, and that is why they were saved without any favoritism.

keyTerms.meaning: for appearance, only on the outside
the Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: הֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים —
phrases.english: He said to them: They only did it for appearance,
so too the Holy One, Blessed be He,
only acted with them for appearance.
phrases.notes: ה׳ threatened them with the decree but never meant to carry it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Measure for measure: the punishment matched the outward-only nature of the sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their idol worship was real, so being saved would be favoritism.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their bowing was only outward, so ה׳'s decree was only a threat, and saving them was fair.

steps.title: A פסוק shows ה׳ does not punish from His heart
steps.stepSummary: The idea is supported by the פסוק in איכה: 'For He does not afflict from His heart.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is what is written: 'For He does not afflict from His heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to back up רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳'s suffering is not 'from His heart,' meaning He does not truly want it. That matches the idea that the decree in the מגילה was only for show.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written
from His heart, truly wanting it

steps.whatToRemember: The Jews of that generation deserved destruction because they bowed to the idol. Since they did it only for show, ה׳ only threatened them and then saved them.

phrases.english: And this is what is written: 'For He does not afflict from His heart.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מגילת איכה, chapter 3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer given in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳'s decree against them was only for show.

steps.title: Courtyard, garden, palace: each guest seated by importance
steps.stepSummary: On the words 'in the court of the garden of the king's palace,' one of רב and שמואל says each guest was seated in the place that fit his rank.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the court of the garden of the king's palace.' רב and שמואל disagree. One says: whoever fit the courtyard went to the courtyard, whoever fit the garden went to the garden, and whoever fit the palace went to the palace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to explaining the words of the מגילה, this time the three places named for the feast. The first opinion says the guests were divided by importance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names three places, so the question is how they relate. According to this view, all three were used at once, with the most important guests in the palace, the next level in the garden, and the simpler guests in the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who is fit for

phrases.english: 'In the court of the garden of the king's palace.'
phrases.notes: This is from the מגילה, describing where the second feast for the people of שושן was held.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree. One said:
whoever was fit for the courtyard went to the courtyard,
whoever was fit for the garden went to the garden,
whoever was fit for the palace went to the palace.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בַּחֲצַר גִּנַּת בִּיתַן הַמֶּלֶךְ״. רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to explaining the פסוקים about the second feast (from step 12), after the side discussion in steps 15-21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three places were used together, and each guest was seated according to his importance.

steps.title: The other view: the crowd kept moving until there was room
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion says the guests were first put in the courtyard, then the garden, and only the palace was big enough to hold them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one says: He seated them in the courtyard, but it didn't hold them; in the garden, but it didn't hold them; until he brought them into the palace and it held them.
steps.whatsHappening: The second of רב and שמואל gives a different explanation of the three places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the places are not used at the same time by rank. They were tried one after another because the crowd was so big, and only the palace was large enough.

keyTerms.meaning: it held them, had room for them

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: הוֹשִׁיבָן בֶּחָצֵר וְלֹא הֶחְזִיקָתַן,
phrases.english: And the other said: He seated them in the courtyard, but it did not hold them,
in the garden, but it did not hold them,
until he brought them into the palace, and it held them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: הוֹשִׁיבָן בֶּחָצֵר וְלֹא הֶחְזִיקָתַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the dispute begun in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The places were tried one after another because of the huge crowd, and only the palace could hold everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא: seated in the courtyard with doors to garden and palace
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a third explanation. The guests sat in the courtyard, which had two doorways, one to the garden and one to the palace.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: He seated them in the courtyard and opened two doorways for them, one to the garden and one to the palace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third way of reading the פסוק, taught in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view everyone sat in the courtyard, but they had open access to both the garden and the palace. That explains why the פסוק mentions all three places.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
He seated them in the courtyard
and opened two doorways for them,
one to the garden and one to the palace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third explanation alongside the two views in steps 22-23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guests sat in the courtyard with open doorways to the garden and the palace.

steps.title: What does the word חור mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'חור כרפס ותכלת' from the מגילה and asks what חור means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'חור, כרפס and תכלת.' What is חור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק, which lists the fabrics used to decorate the feast. It asks about the unclear word חור, setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חור is an unusual word, so the גמרא needs to define it. The answers are given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a fabric named in the מגילה (meaning explained next)

phrases.english: 'Chur, karpas, and sky-blue.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק describes the fabric hangings that decorated the feast.

phrases.english: What is chur?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the description of the feast.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word חור.

steps.title: רב: full of holes; שמואל: white wool
steps.stepSummary: רב says חור means fabric full of holes, like lace. שמואל says it means white wool spread out for the guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: holes upon holes. And שמואל says: he spread white wool out for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל each give a meaning for the word חור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב connects חור to the word for 'hole' (חור), so a fabric full of holes, like lace. שמואל connects it to the word for 'white,' so white wool coverings.

phrases.english: Rav said: holes upon holes,
phrases.notes: He means a fabric full of little holes, something like lace.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מֵילָת לְבָנָה הִצִּיעַ לָהֶם.
phrases.english: and Shmuel said: He spread out white wool for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: fabric full of holes. שמואל: white wool spread out for the guests.

steps.title: כרפס means cushions of velvet
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains כרפס as כרים של פסים, cushions made of velvet.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'כרפס': רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: cushions of velvet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next fabric word in the פסוק, כרפס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר חנינא splits the word into two parts: כר (cushion) and פס (velvet). This shows how fancy the decorations at the feast were.

keyTerms.meaning: a fabric named in the מגילה

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא explains the feast's seating (by rank, by crowd size, or courtyard with doorways) and its fancy fabrics: חור is lace-like or white wool, and כרפס is velvet cushions.

phrases.english: 'Karpas': Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
cushions of velvet.
phrases.notes: He is splitting the word in two: כר (cushion) plus פס (velvet).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the words of the same פסוק from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כרפס means velvet cushions (כרים של פסים).

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Gold couches for important guests, silver for the rest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the פסוק about gold and silver couches. A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה, who says each guest got a couch that matched his importance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'On silver rods and marble pillars, couches of gold and silver.' A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says a guest fit for silver sat on silver, and a guest fit for gold sat on gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the מגילה and brings רבי יהודה's explanation of why there were both gold and silver couches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions two metals, so רבי יהודה reads it as two kinds of couches. The more important guests got gold and the less important got silver.

keyTerms.meaning: Couches or beds that guests reclined on at a feast
The one who is fit for, deserving of

phrases.english: "On silver rods and pillars of marble,
couches of gold and silver"
phrases.notes: This is still אסתר א:ו, the same פסוק the גמרא has been explaining.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The one fit for silver sat on silver,
the one fit for gold sat on gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the next words of the same פסוק after כרפס (Step 27).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were two kinds of couches, gold for important guests and silver for others.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: That would make guests jealous
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה pushes back: if some guests got gold and others silver, people would be jealous at the feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: If so, you are throwing jealousy into the feast.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי יהודה's explanation. A king throwing a party to please people would not split guests in a way that causes jealousy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on logic, not on the wording of the פסוק. Ranking guests by gold and silver would ruin the happy mood the king wanted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, אַתָּה מֵטִיל קִנְאָה בַּסְּעוּדָה.
phrases.english: If so, you are casting jealousy into the feast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אַתָּה מֵטִיל קִנְאָה בַּסְּעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly argues against רבי יהודה's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading that guests got different couches by rank
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Giving some guests better couches than others would make the guests jealous, which a host would never want.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's reading: Silver couches with gold legs
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה gives his own explanation: every couch was silver, and every couch had gold legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the couches themselves were silver and their legs were gold.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי יהודה, רבי נחמיה explains the two metals in a way that keeps all guests equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both gold and silver are still in each couch, so the פסוק's two metals are explained. But now every guest gets the same couch, so no one is jealous.

phrases.english: Rather: they themselves were of silver,
and their legs were of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי נחמיה replaces the rejected reading with his own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gold and silver meant two different kinds of couches for different guests.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each couch was made of both metals: silver body, gold legs, so all guests were equal.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: gold couches for important guests, silver for others. רבי נחמיה: that causes jealousy, so every couch was silver with gold legs.

steps.title: רבי אסי: בהט means stones people long to own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the word בהט. רבי אסי says these are stones so precious that people work hard to get them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'בהט and marble.' רבי אסי said: These are stones that make their owners eager for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next unclear word in the פסוק, בהט, which describes the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי does not name a specific stone. He explains it as stones so valuable that people are willing to pay a lot to own them.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of precious stone in the floor of the feast
That make people eager or longing for them

phrases.english: "Bahat and marble."
phrases.notes: Still the same פסוק. This is describing the floor the guests walked on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
Stones that make their owners long for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the couches to the next word in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בהט are very precious stones that people eagerly want to own.

steps.title: Support from Zechariah: Crown stones glittering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי brings a פסוק from זכריה that also describes precious stones in a similar way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it says: 'Crown stones, glittering over His land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי backs up his explanation with another פסוק that uses similar language about precious stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in זכריה compares the Jewish people to stones of a crown. It shows that the תנ״ך describes precious stones as something prized and admired, which fits רבי אסי's reading of בהט.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (introducing a supporting פסוק)

phrases.english: And so it says:
"Stones of a crown, glittering over His land."
phrases.notes: This is from זכריה ט:טז, where the Jewish people are compared to precious crown jewels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a supporting פסוק for רבי אסי's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's reading of בהט as precious, prized stones
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה ט:טז, 'אבני נזר מתנוססות על אדמתו'

steps.title: רב: דר means many rows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains דר וסוחרת. רב says it means rows upon rows of stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And דר and סוחרת.' רב said: Rows and rows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last words of the פסוק and starts a list of three explanations. This is the first one, from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads דר as related to rows going around. The floor stones were laid in many rows circling around.

keyTerms.meaning: Last two unclear words in the פסוק describing the floor

phrases.english: "And dar and socharet,"
Rav said: Rows and rows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דר וסוחרת means the floor had many rows of stones going around.

steps.title: שמואל: A glowing gem called דרה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a second explanation: דר is a precious stone named דרה that lit up the whole feast like midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: There is a precious stone in the sea cities called דרה. He placed it in the middle of the feast and it lit things up for them like noon.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and reads דר as the name of a specific glowing gem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, דר describes the floor's design. For שמואל, it is an actual stone that gave off light, so the feast was bright like the middle of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Big cities by the sea, seaports
Like midday, as bright as noon

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
There is a precious stone in the seaports,
and its name is "dara,"
he placed it in the middle of the feast,
phrases.notes: "He" is אחשורוש.

phrases.english: and it lit up for them like midday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different explanation of the same words that רב explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דר is a glowing gem named דרה that lit the feast like noon.

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: Freedom for all merchants
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: the words mean the king declared freedom for all merchants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: He proclaimed freedom for all merchants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third explanation of דר וסוחרת, which is not about the floor at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here דר is read like דרור, freedom, and סוחרת like סוחר, merchant. So the king gave the merchants a break, freeing them from what they owed, in honor of the feast.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
That he proclaimed freedom for all merchants.
phrases.notes: They hear דר as דרור (freedom) and סוחרת as סוחר (merchant). The merchants were let off from paying their taxes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the same words after רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דר וסוחרת means the king declared freedom for all merchants.
steps.whatToRemember: Three readings of דר וסוחרת: רב says rows of stones, שמואל says a glowing gem, and the school of רבי ישמעאל says freedom for merchants.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say שונים and not משונים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק about the cups and asks why it uses the word שונים instead of the more fitting משונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they gave drink in gold vessels, and vessels different from vessels.' It should have said משונים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices odd wording in the פסוק and points out that a different word would have been more correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משונים is the normal word for 'different.' Since the פסוק chose שונים, the גמרא assumes it is hinting at something extra.

phrases.english: "And they gave drink in vessels of gold,
and vessels different from vessels."
phrases.notes: This is the next פסוק, אסתר א:ז.

phrases.english: It should have said "meshunim"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in the description of the feast.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word שונים in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proper word for 'different' is משונים, so the פסוק's choice of שונים needs explaining.

steps.title: רבא: A heavenly voice said 'you are repeating the sin'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that שונים hints at repeating. A בת קול said the earlier ones were destroyed for using the בית המקדש's vessels, and now you use them again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A בת קול came out and said to them: The earlier ones were destroyed because of My vessels, and you are using them again!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reading שונים as 'repeating,' not just 'different.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels were the כלי המקדש. The earlier ones who used them were destroyed, and אחשורוש's guests were doing the same thing again. So the odd word is a warning from heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Were destroyed, came to an end

phrases.english: Rava said,
A heavenly voice came out and said to them:
The earlier ones were destroyed because of My vessels,
phrases.notes: The earlier ones are people like בלשאצר, who used the vessels of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and you are repeating with them!
phrases.notes: Here שונים means 'doing it again,' which is why the פסוק used that word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the פסוק said שונים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the unusual word as a hidden message
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שונים just means 'different' and is the wrong word.
steps.terutzMaskana: שונים means 'repeating': they were using the בית המקדש's vessels again, after earlier users were destroyed for it.
steps.confusionAlert: שונים here does not just mean 'different.' רבא reads it from the root meaning 'to do again.'

steps.title: רב: Each guest got wine older than himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'יין מלכות רב.' רב says each guest was served wine that was older than he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And royal wine in abundance (רב).' רב said: This teaches that every single guest was given wine older than himself in years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק, reading the word רב as 'older.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב can mean 'plenty,' but רב reads it as 'greater,' meaning older. So the king served every guest well-aged wine that was older than that guest.

phrases.english: "And royal wine, abundant,"
Rav said:
This teaches that each and every one was given to drink
wine that was older than him in years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each guest was served wine older than himself.

steps.title: What does 'according to the law' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the drinking at the feast and asks what the word כדת means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the drinking was according to the law; none did compel.' What does 'according to the law' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק and asks what the word כדת is telling us. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Which 'law' could a drinking party possibly follow? The word seems out of place, so the גמרא wants to know what rule the feast was following.

phrases.english: "And the drinking was according to the law (none did compel)"
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, which finish the פסוק. The גמרא comes back to them in a moment.

phrases.english: What is "according to the law"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'יין מלכות רב' to the next phrase in the same פסוק sequence.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which 'law' the drinking at the feast followed.

steps.title: The feast followed the תורה's pattern: more food than drink
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן, quoting רבי מאיר, says כדת means the תורה's law: just as קרבנות have more food than drink, the feast had more food than drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said in the name of רבי מאיר: According to the law of the תורה. Just as in the תורה's law the food is more than the drink, so too at that wicked man's feast the food was more than the drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנן answers the question: 'the law' means the תורה's law. At the feast, as with קרבנות, there was more food than drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קרבנות on the מזבח, the animal or flour offering is large and the wine poured with it (נסכים) is small. The feast copied that proportion, so it was not just a drinking party.

keyTerms.meaning: The food is more than the drink

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
According to the law of the Torah.
Just as with the law of the Torah
the food is more than the drink,
phrases.notes: He means קרבנות. The offering on the מזבח is much bigger than the bit of wine poured alongside it.

phrases.english: so too at the feast of that wicked man
phrases.notes: 'That wicked man' is אחשורוש.

phrases.english: the food was more than the drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כדת means the Torah's pattern of food outweighing drink, as with קרבנות and נסכים.

steps.title: No one was forced: each guest drank his own country's wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains 'אין אונס' to mean that every guest was served wine from his own country.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'None did compel.' רבי אלעזר said: This teaches that each and every guest was given wine from his own country to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק, 'אין אונס,' and רבי אלעזר explains what they mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No compulsion' could just mean no one had to drink. רבי אלעזר reads it more specifically: no one had to drink a foreign wine he did not like, because each guest got the wine of his homeland.

keyTerms.meaning: None did compel; no one was forced
The wine of his own country

phrases.english: "None did compel":
Rabbi Elazar said:
This teaches that each and every one
was given to drink from the wine of his own country.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the phrase quoted in step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אין אונס' means each guest drank wine from his own country.

steps.title: 'Every man's pleasure' means the wishes of מרדכי and המן
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'איש ואיש' as two specific men, מרדכי and המן, whose wishes guided the feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To do according to the wish of man and man.' רבא said: To do according to the wishes of מרדכי and המן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the פסוק, and רבא says the 'man and man' are two particular people: מרדכי and המן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'איש ואיש' means 'each person.' רבא reads it as 'a man and a man,' meaning two specific people the feast followed. The next step shows why those two are called 'איש.'

keyTerms.meaning: Man and man; can also mean every man

phrases.english: "To do according to the wish of man and man":
phrases.notes: Usually this is read as 'each man's wish.' רבא reads it as two particular men.

phrases.english: Rava said:
To do according to the wishes of Mordecai and Haman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹן מָרְדֳּכַי וְהָמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the final phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'איש ואיש' refers to מרדכי and המן.

steps.title: Both מרדכי and המן are called 'איש' in the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבא's reading by showing that the מגילה calls both מרדכי and המן 'איש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מרדכי, as it is written: 'a Jewish man.' המן: 'a man who is an adversary and an enemy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings פסוקים to back up רבא, showing that each of these two people is called 'איש' elsewhere in the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי is called 'איש יהודי' (אסתר ב:ה), and המן is called 'איש צר ואויב' (אסתר ז:ו). Because each one carries the title 'איש,' the doubled 'איש ואיש' can point to the two of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who is an adversary and an enemy (said of המן)

phrases.english: Mordecai, as it is written: "A Jewish man";
phrases.notes: This is from אסתר ב:ה, where מרדכי is first introduced.

phrases.english: Haman: "A man who is an adversary and an enemy."
phrases.notes: This is from אסתר ז:ו, when אסתר names המן in front of the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural basis for רבא's reading in step 42.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that 'איש ואיש' means מרדכי and המן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אסתר ב:ה ('איש יהודי') and אסתר ז:ו ('איש צר ואויב').

steps.title: Why was the women's feast held in the royal house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about ושתי's feast and asks why it was in the 'בית המלכות' and not in the women's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Also ושתי the queen made a feast for the women in the royal house.' It should have said 'the women's house'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק, about ושתי's party, and points out a strange detail: a women's feast held in the king's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A feast for women would naturally take place in the women's quarters, which the מגילה itself calls 'בית הנשים.' The פסוק's choice of 'בית המלכות,' the men's royal area, seems out of place, and the גמרא wants an explanation.

phrases.english: "Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women
in the royal house."
It should have said "the women's house"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק (אסתר א:ט) in the running commentary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'בית המלכות' in אסתר א:ט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A women's feast belongs in the women's quarters, so the פסוק should have said 'בית הנשים.'

steps.title: Both אחשורוש and ושתי had sinful intentions
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that both the king and the queen intended sin, and he starts quoting a folk saying about a husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both of them intended to sin. This is what people say: He with pumpkins, and his wife...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the odd location: ושתי put her feast near the men because, like her husband, she had sinful aims. He begins a popular saying that continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחשורוש wanted to sin with the women, and ושתי wanted to sin with the men, so she held her party in the men's royal area. The folk saying describes a husband and wife who each pursue the same kind of wrongdoing.
steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of the saying ('and his wife...'). Nothing is missing from your text; the rest of the saying appears in the next section.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The two of them intended to sin.
phrases.notes: He means the king wanted the women and ושתי wanted the men, which is why she held her party near them.

phrases.english: This is what people say:
He with pumpkins, and his wife
phrases.notes: The saying is cut off here. It finishes on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁנֵיהֶן לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה נִתְכַּוְּונוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 44.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the unusual wording through the characters' hidden intentions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'בית המלכות' location seemed out of place for a women's feast.
steps.terutzMaskana: ושתי chose the men's royal house on purpose, because she, like אחשורוש, intended to sin.
